messages.author: 9ece5b53e5e84d20
messages.subject: Question about `inla.spde2.matern` priors
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to reproduce the analysis from a paper that used the `inla.spde2.matern` function. It looks like they haven't set the priors for the hyperparameters associated with the model since they run only:

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=meshfit, alpha=2)
res <- inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stk.full),
                 control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, A=inla.stack.A(stk.full)))

Therefore, I'm trying to figure out the default priors used with this latent model. (I'm aware that it is recommended to use `inla.spde2.pcmatern` instead, but I'm trying to reproduce some analysis from this paper I mentioned.)

When I look into `inla.docs("spde2", section = "latent")`, the documentation from the model is not available. In fact, when I go to the directory where INLA (I'm using version 23.08.18) is installed and ask for a list of files within "documentation/latent", none of the SPDE models is available (take a look below for reference)

> ls documentation/latent
ar.pdf              copy.pdf            intslope.pdf        rw2d-model.pdf
ar1.pdf             crw2.pdf            linear.pdf          rw2d.pdf
ar1c.pdf            dmatern.pdf         log1exp.pdf         rw2diid.pdf
besag.pdf           fgn.pdf             logdist.pdf         rw2dx3-model.pdf
besag2.pdf          generic0.pdf        matern2d.pdf        scopy.pdf
besagproper-OLD.pdf generic1.pdf        meb.pdf             seasonal.pdf
besagproper.pdf     generic2.pdf        mec-details.pdf     sigm.pdf
besagproper2.pdf    generic3.pdf        mec.pdf             slm.pdf
bym.pdf             iid.pdf             ou.pdf              wishard.pdf
bym2.pdf            iid123d.pdf         rgeneric.pdf        z.pdf
cgeneric.pdf        iidkd.pdf           rw1.pdf
clinear.pdf         indep.pdf           rw2.pdf

I noticed the default priors for the latent model "matern2d" (matern on a lattice) are
log(tau) \sim log-gamma(1, 5e-05), and
log(range) \sim log-gamma(1, 0.01).

My question is, do the same default priors hold for `inla.spde2.matern`?

Thanks,
Lucas.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about `inla.spde2.matern` priors
parts:
The priors for the internal “theta” parameters can be found via inla.models()$latent$spde2, I think, but that won’t be very helpful for you, since the internal representation depends on some of the arguments to inla.spde2.matern() itself.
I think we did write about the default priors in the JSS paper on the spde2 interface, although we there promoted an alternative approach where one would explicitly parameterise the model in terms of log(range) and log(variance) instead of log(kappa) and log(tau).  Nowadays, the pcmatern implementation essentially uses the alternative approach (but with std.dev. instead of variance.  In hindsight, I wish I wouldn’t have allowed any default priors for inla.spde2.matern()…
It should however be more clear if you follow the code itself; I can take a look when I’m at my computer next.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about `inla.spde2.matern` priors
parts:
Hi,
I took a look at the code, and the default parameter setup for inla.spde2.matern is in the param2.matern.orig() function. The default nominal variance is set to 1, meaning it tries to set the prior median for the marginal variance to 1. The default prior median range is constructed to be the approximate mesh diameter divided by 5 ( *0.2 in the code). The default prior precision on the log scale is 0.1.
If you want to replicate results where they’ve used the default settings, you’ll therefore need the same mesh, or at least know its approximate diameter. For details of the default prior construction, see the code, in rinla/R/spde2.R of the r-inla git repo.

Finn
